## Goal (user story)

As a developer/QA, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode (extending MainStreetMonteCarlo) that runs ≥200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics, so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.

## Context

`MainStreetMonteCarlo` is single-player only (`runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` with one strategy × one difficulty per run). Competitive mode needs head-to-head metrics: both players' win/score distributions plus per-player diagnostics. Architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner), but the harness validates the head-to-head (human vs 1 AI) path initially; N>2 extension is a future parameterisation.

## Scope

- Head-to-head harness extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (new entry point or flag): both players act per shared-day, same seed → deterministic head-to-head run.
- ≥200 seeds; outputs win/score distributions plus per-player metrics (wins per owner, average score per owner, draw/early-end handling).
- Single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Out of scope

- AI strategy itself (sibling).
- Per-owner income routing (sibling).
- Rendering / scene (AC5 child).
- Endless continuation (deferred).
- N>2 Monte Carlo — harness is N-player-extensible (numOpponents param) but AC4 validates head-to-head; broader N is a follow-up.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Head-to-head harness runs ≥200 seeds with deterministic head-to-head execution (same seed → same per-owner outcome) and produces win/score distributions (win rate per owner, median/average score per owner).
- [ ] **AC2:** Per-player metrics include at least wins, average score, and loss-reason distribution per owner plus a deterministic summary (draw/early-end handling documented).
- [ ] **AC3:** Extension of `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (not a replacement); existing `runMonteCarlo` / `runAllCombinations` and `monte-carlo-balance.test.ts` still pass.
- [ ] **AC4:** Validated against the adapted competitive AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness extension (win/score distributions, per-player metrics).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-monte-carlo.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive Monte Carlo tests (determinism, distributions, guardrails).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30
- Depends on: competitive state model + phase machine + income routing + AI strategy (CG-0MT5X3N79002S038)
- Architecture: N-player-ready state/phase; harness parametrises head-to-head initially

AC5 of the parent epic is engine-only: no game-selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome. # Add a Charity Shop business card (MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

Main Street has no charity shop: a low-cost, Culture-synergy business that trades a modest income for a steady reputation trickle. The producer has specified the card's core economy (1.5 income/turn, 0.15 reputation/turn, cost 3 at the pre-scale convention), and this work adds the card to the pool so players gain an early reputation-leaning Culture business at tier 2.

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I can buy a Charity Shop for 300 coins and place it on the street, where it produces a small income and a steady reputation gain each turn, giving me an early Culture-synergy building with a reputation focus.
- **As a player**, I expect the Charity Shop to participate in Culture adjacency synergy like other Culture businesses (Bookshop, Craft Shop), so I can cluster it with my Culture cards.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect the new card to be a first-class registered template — present in the CSV, the tier/progression system, generated metadata and card art — with all template-count and consistency tests updated rather than special-cased.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data.** `src/card-data.csv` contains a new business row with exactly: `family = business`, `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 150`, `synergyTypes = Culture`, `upgradePath` empty (standalone), `maxLevel = 0`, `reputationPerTurn = 15`, `ongoingCost = 75`, `tier = 2`, plus a non-empty `description` and `art_notes`. (**Producer-accepted variance, 2026-10-01:** the card is standalone — `upgradePath` empty and `maxLevel = 0` — matching the repo convention for standalone businesses (Craft Shop, Pharmacy, Grand Hotel); the earlier `upgradePath = Charity Shop` / `maxLevel = 1` wording was self-contradictory since no matching upgrade card exists.)
2. **Registered template.** The card is loaded by `MainStreetCards.ts` as a business template, is available at tier 2 through the tier/`CARD_TIER_MAP` progression, and appears in the business deck built by `createBusinessDeck()`.
3. **Generated metadata and art.** `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` lists `biz-charity-shop` under `expandedCardIds.business`, and `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` produces `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-charity-shop.svg`; both are committed.
4. **Tests.** Automated tests assert the Charity Shop's `cost`, `baseIncome`, `reputationPerTurn`, `ongoingCost`, `synergyTypes` and `tier`, and every hardcoded count affected by adding one business template is updated:
   - business-template count `30 → 31` in `game-state.test.ts` (`BUSINESS_TEMPLATE_COUNT`), `expanded-card-pool.test.ts`, `group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` (test title/comment too), and the `createBusinessDeck(1).length` assertions in the `group-b`…`group-f` expansion tests;
   - aggregate pool totals in `meta-progression.test.ts`: tier-12 `cumulativeCardIds` `173 → 174` and unique base-id `allBaseIds.size` `165 → 166`;
   - the hardcoded tier-2 synergy snapshot in `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` becomes `{ Commerce: 2, Service: 1, Culture: 1 }`.
   The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (business table, deck-size/expansion counts, synergy-type coverage) and any relevant README or docs-site entries. **Note:** `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **×100 integer economy** (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6): all coin/reputation CSV values are integers at 100× the design scale — `cost 300`, `baseIncome 150`, `reputationPerTurn 15`. No fractional values anywhere in the CSV.
- **Ongoing cost convention** (CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE): businesses pay ¼ of purchase price per turn (min 25), so `ongoingCost = 75`; the card is charged this while in hand or on the street.
- **Card text must match data** (`card-text-data-consistency` test): the `description` reputation figure must equal the `reputationPerTurn` value and the synergy sentence must match the Culture synergy.
- **Tier-2 synergy balance** (`tier-synergy-balance.test.ts`, ≤2× ratio): tier 2 becomes Commerce 2 / Service 1 / Culture 1 — ratio 2.0, which passes.
- **Tier family balance** (`tier-family-balance.test.ts`, ≤46% per family): tier 2 business share becomes 4/22 ≈ 18.2% — passes.
- **Producer-specified cost override:** the balance curve (`tier*2 + 2 + baseIncome*4 + …`) would price this card higher than 300; the producer's explicit `cost 3` (300) takes precedence and is recorded as a deliberate manual override, not a curve result.

## Existing state

- There is **no** charity shop / thrift / op-shop card in `card-data.csv` or `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`; this is a net-new template.
- The pool currently has **30 business templates**; tier 2 contains Hardware Store (Service), Pawn Shop (Commerce) and Boutique (Commerce).
- Business cards are generic CSV-driven templates; `MainStreetCards.ts` parses rows, and per-tier registration is derived from the CSV `tier` column (`CARD_TIER_MAP`) — no bespoke TypeScript class is needed.
- Tests hardcode both the business-template count (`30`) **and aggregate pool totals** (tier-12 cumulative `173`, unique base-id set `165`), and `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` enumerates every non-baseline business id (currently 26 business ids; with the 4 tier-1 baseline business ids the total is 30) — all must be updated. `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` also hardcodes the per-tier synergy snapshot.
- Business card art resolves through `card-art-map.json` with a generic `Fallback` sprite when a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite is absent.

## Desired change

Add the Charity Shop as a tier-2 Culture business template with the values in AC1, regenerate the derived metadata and SVG card artifacts, update the hardcoded business-count assertions and the catalog documentation, and add/extend tests asserting the new card's economy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — add the `biz-charity-shop` business row.
- `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — regenerate via `npx vite-node src/scripts/generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` (business id list grows 26 → 27).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-charity-shop.svg` — generated by `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — add the card to the tier-2 business table; update the two deck-size tables (Business 30 → 31, business cards 90 → 93), the expansion summary (Business 30 → 31, total 157 → 158, net +142 → +143) and the synergy-type coverage table (Culture single 4 → 5; Culture total 10 → 11).
- `tests/main-street/game-state.test.ts` — `BUSINESS_TEMPLATE_COUNT` 30 → 31.
- `tests/main-street/group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` — business template count 30 → 31 (and wording/comment).
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — business template count 30 → 31 (and test description).
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts`, `group-c-investment-events-expansion.test.ts`, `group-d-incident-events-expansion.test.ts`, `group-e-upgrade-cards-expansion.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` — `createBusinessDeck(1).length` 30 → 31.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — tier-12 `cumulativeCardIds` 173 → 174 (test title/comment too) and `allBaseIds.size` 165 → 166.
- `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` — extend the hardcoded sparse-tier snapshot for `'tier-2'` with `Culture: 1` (and update the header comment); optionally add a Charity Shop synergy assertion.
- `tests/main-street/card-manifest.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/card-svg-coverage.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tier-family-balance.test.ts` — driven by the regenerated artifacts/CSV; verify they pass.
- `tests/main-street/card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — verifies card text matches data; passes once `description`/`art_notes` match the values in AC1.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — add a Special Cases note for the producer's manual cost override (if the balance doc is maintained against the CSV).

## Related work

> The `CG-` ids below are from the legacy Tableau-Card-Engine (core) worklog; the same content was migrated to this repo under the `MS-` prefix (see the migration comment on this item).

- `CG-0MUAYBA0L000XLK3` — Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (sibling migrated producer note; establishes the ×100 value convention for business cards).
- `CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6` — integer economy (coin/rep ×100).
- `CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE` — business ongoing cost (¼ purchase price, min 25).
- `CG-0MUIH30NQ0047W1I` — Reconcile event card text to integer data; `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` — validate all card text.
- `CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB` — tier synergy-type balance rule (constrains tier-2 placement).
- `CG-0MT3C744B009DS84` / `CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143` — 12-tier progression and family rebalance.
- Automated related-work report: `CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY` (Main Street: design 50+ new cards), `CG-0MMJTGQFE1RL6VJA` (synergy icons in help panel).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q2):** synergy type is **Culture** (a charity shop might thematically read as Commerce; overridden by the producer's answer).
- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q3; wording corrected on acceptance of the AC1 variance 2026-10-01):** **tier 2, standalone** (`upgradePath` empty, `maxLevel = 0`, no upgrade chain).
- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q1):** 1.5 is **gross** `baseIncome`; the standard 75 ongoing cost applies on top (net 0.75/turn).
- **Assumption (not explicitly confirmed; low risk):** `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, and house-style `description`/`art_notes` text; the card uses the generic fallback sprite until dedicated art is supplied.
- **Risk:** hardcoded business counts **and aggregate pool totals** are spread across many tests; missing one turns the suite red — the count updates are the largest part of the change.
- **Risk:** regenerating `expanded-card-manifest.json` and SVG artifacts produces large/generated diffs; regenerate via the documented scripts rather than hand-editing.
- **Scope-creep guard:** dedicated 1024×1024 artwork for the card is **out of scope**; if wanted, record it as a linked follow-up work item rather than expanding this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1: Are the stated numbers gross or net of the standard ongoing cost?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): A** — 1.5 is gross `baseIncome`; `baseIncome = 150`, `ongoingCost = 75`, net 0.75/turn. Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4` on this item.
- **Q2: Which synergy type should the Charity Shop belong to?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): C** — `Culture`. Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4`.
- **Q3: Which progression tier, and should it have an upgrade path?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): A** — `tier = 2`, standalone. The literal `upgradePath = Charity Shop`, `maxLevel = 1` values carried in from the originating intake were incorrect for a standalone card and were corrected to `upgradePath` empty / `maxLevel = 0`; the producer **accepted this variance on 2026-10-01** (see the producer acceptance comment on this item). Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4`.
- **Note:** these answers were carried over from the originating (core-repo) intake; the producer should confirm them alongside the corrected paths/counts at the next review.
- **Non-blocking assumptions:** `id`/`name`/`description`/`art_notes` and fallback-art usage were proposed in the questions comment and **not corrected** by the producer; they are treated as accepted defaults unless the producer objects.

# Write storylines — harden, document, and extend the Main Street storyline system

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-09-26): **Q1 = epic**; **Q2 = implement all
improvements now**; **Q3 = keep Main Street-specific, but design with an eye to
extracting into core-engine in future — cutting corners is acceptable now, but
do not make extraction impossible.**

## Problem statement

Main Street has a *rough* storyline implementation: incident event cards can
carry a dual choice (`hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId`)
and the player's Accept/Reject decision schedules the next card in a chain
(`CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128`). The mechanic works and is tested, but it is thin,
implicit, and undocumented:

- the branching model supports only binary choices with one successor per
  branch, with no storyline identity/grouping;
- there is no static validation — a dangling chain link is only logged at
  runtime (`Chain card X not found in card data.`);
- there is no authoring, validation, or visualisation tooling (chains are
  hand-edited inside a 155-row CSV);
- no documentation explains how storylines are created and managed; and
- storylines are invisible to players as stories — they see two opaque
  buttons and no memory of how their choices shaped events.

This makes storylines hard to extend safely and invisible as a source of
player agency.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — author, extend and balance storylines
  (new chains, retro-fitting existing incidents) without editing engine code,
  and see the shape of a storyline at a glance.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need a documented, validated, and
  flexible data model with clear seams so storyline changes cannot silently
  break, and so the mechanic can later move to the core engine.
- **Players** — should feel their choices shape an unfolding story, with
  visible continuity (what they chose, what it led to, which thread is still
  running) rather than two opaque buttons.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — need a decision policy that remains correct as the
  branching model and option counts grow.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to define a storyline declaratively and run a
  validator, so I know every branch resolves before I ship it."
- "As a developer, I want a documented storyline model and an authoring guide,
  so I can add a multi-step chain without reverse-engineering the engine."
- "As a player, I want a storyline journal that shows my past choices and what
  they led to, so my decisions feel like they build a narrative."
- "As a player, I want to know which story threads are still running, so
  recurring events feel connected rather than random."
- "As a producer, I want a prioritised roadmap of further storyline
  improvements, so I can schedule the next iteration."

## Scope areas (all to be implemented — Q2 = all now)

### A. Model & engine hardening (+ future extraction seam)

1. **Storyline identity/grouping** — optional `storylineId` (+ display
   `storylineTitle`) on `EventCard` and in the CSV, grouping chain cards into
   named storylines. Backward compatible.
2. **Generalised option model** — support an ordered list of options (each
   with a label, a successor card id, and an effect policy of apply/skip),
   while preserving legacy `hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` /
   `rejectNextCardId` semantics byte-for-byte.
3. **Extraction seam** — isolate storyline definitions, state and resolution
   behind a small game-agnostic interface/registry and pure functions, with
   migration notes, so the mechanic can move to `src/core-engine` later
   without rewriting callers. Corners may be cut, but the boundary must exist
   and be documented.
4. **Static validation** — every link resolves; no dangling, duplicate or
   unknown references; sinks and cycles are intentional. Validation fails
   loudly (non-zero exit), not just via a runtime log.
5. **Invariants preserved** — undo/redo, save/load (old saves load), deferred
   end-of-turn mutation, transcript shape and AI resolution stay correct for
   all option counts.

### B. Documentation

6. Canonical **`docs/main-street/storylines.md`**: concepts, data model + CSV
   columns, resolution lifecycle, AI policy, tooling usage, an end-to-end
   authoring walkthrough with a worked example, an authoring checklist, and a
   documented extraction path to core-engine.
7. **`docs/DEVELOPER.md`** and **`example-games/main-street/README.md`**
   cross-reference the doc and list the new CSV columns and scripts.
8. A **doc-drift test** asserts the docs exist and that documented chain
   examples match the shipped CSV.
9. A prioritised **future-improvements roadmap** (tooling + player agency)
   documenting anything deliberately deferred, with deferred ideas captured as
   work items.

### C. Tooling (implemented)

10. **Validator** — `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` + an npm script
    (`validate:storylines`), wired into the test suite / pre-push so
    regressions fail the build.
11. **Graph / manifest export** — tool to emit a storyline graph or manifest
    (`--format mermaid|json`) plus a committed generated artefact and a JSON
    schema.
12. **Authoring helper** — a CLI (or equivalent documented commands) to add and
    link storyline cards safely, without hand-editing CSV internals.

### D. Player agency (implemented)

13. **Named storylines surfaced** in the choice dialog and activity log.
14. **Storyline journal/history overlay** — review past choices and outcomes,
    accessible from the HUD, using the standard overlay pattern and
    reduced-motion behaviour, backed by the existing transcript/log.
15. **Choice clarity** — explanatory tooltips/labels for each option that
    explain consequence semantics **without** revealing the escalation card
    (preserving the designed tension).
16. **Outcome feedback** — each resolved choice produces a concise narrative
    "story update" line tied to its `storylineId`.
17. **Continuity / foreshadowing** — an active/recurring-thread indicator while
    a storyline is in play (including cycles).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storyline metadata** — `EventCard` (and the CSV) supports an optional
   `storylineId` and `storylineTitle`; the parser populates them; cards
   without them behave exactly as before. Covered by unit tests.
2. **Generalised option model** — the engine supports an arbitrary ordered
   list of options (label, successor card id, effect policy apply/skip);
   legacy `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` cards resolve
   identically. Covered by unit tests proving legacy-equivalence and a
   multi-option resolution.
3. **Extraction seam** — storyline definition/state/resolution are behind a
   documented game-agnostic interface/registry boundary with pure functions
   and explicit migration notes in the docs; no caller reaches into
   Main-Street-only internals for resolution.
4. **Static validation passes** — every `acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId`
   (and any new option link) in `card-data.csv` resolves to an existing card;
   no dangling/duplicate/unknown references; validation exits non-zero on
   failure and is enforced in the test suite or pre-push hook.
5. **Invariants preserved** — undo/redo, save/load (old saves without new
   fields load), deferred end-of-turn mutation, transcript `event-choice`
   records, and AI resolution remain correct for all option counts; covered by
   unit tests.

6. **Canonical documentation** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` exists and
   documents concepts, the data model and CSV columns, the resolution
   lifecycle (deferred `pendingEventChoice`, option paths, deck insertion,
   undo/redo, save/load, transcript), the AI policy, tooling usage, a
   step-by-step authoring walkthrough with a worked example, an authoring
   checklist, and the core-engine extraction path.
7. **Cross-references updated** — `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and
   `example-games/main-street/README.md` reference the new doc and list the new
   CSV columns and scripts.
8. **Doc-drift guard** — at least one test/lint asserts the canonical doc
   exists and that its documented chain examples match the shipped CSV.
9. **Future-improvements roadmap** — the documentation contains a prioritised
   roadmap of further tooling and player-agency improvements, and any deferred
   ideas are captured as separate work items.

10. **Validator script** — `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` plus an npm script
    (`validate:storylines`), returning non-zero on invalid storylines and
    covered by tests against both valid and deliberately broken fixtures.
11. **Graph/manifest export** — a tool emits the storyline graph/manifest
    (`--format mermaid|json`); a generated artefact and JSON schema are
    committed, and a test asserts the emitted graph matches the CSV.
12. **Authoring helper** — a documented CLI (or equivalent) can add a
    storyline card/link safely and validate the result; the workflow is covered
    by the authoring guide and at least one test.

13. **Named storylines surfaced** — the choice dialog and activity log show the
    storyline name (e.g. "Tax Troubles — …") when available, with a
    reduced-motion-safe presentation.
14. **Journal/history overlay** — a player can open a storyline journal from
    the HUD that lists past choices and their outcomes; it uses
    `createOverlayBackground`/`createOverlayButton`, parents elements into
    `hudContainer`, and is covered by a browser test.
15. **Choice clarity** — option buttons carry tooltips/labels explaining
    consequence semantics without revealing the escalation card; covered by a
    test.
16. **Outcome feedback** — each resolved choice emits a concise narrative
    "story update" line tied to its storyline; covered by a unit test.
17. **Continuity indicator** — an active/recurring-storyline indicator is
    visible while a storyline is in play and cleared when it ends; covered by a
    test.

18. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
    code comments, `README`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
19. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility** — cards without storyline fields behave exactly
  as before; existing `hasChoices` cards are unchanged; old saves load with
  missing fields defaulted.
- **Determinism / replay safety** — storyline resolution and chain-card
  insertion must not consume RNG or wall-clock time; transcripts stay
  replayable and deterministic.
- **No cost model change** — event choices remain free (no daily-action cost).
- **Preserve designed tension** — choice clarity must not preview the
  escalation card; the "unknown consequence" tension is intentional.
- **Extraction seam, not extraction** — the mechanic stays Main Street-specific
  for now; corners may be cut but the boundaries must not make a later move to
  `src/core-engine` a rewrite.
- **Existing event-flow decisions preserved** — deferred end-of-turn mutation,
  undo/redo semantics, AI difficulty policy and tutorial exclusion of choice
  events must not regress.
- **No new runtime dependency** beyond the existing Node/Vitest/scripts
  toolchain for the tooling.

## Existing state (repo research)

### Data model
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `EventCard` has
  `hasChoices?: boolean`, `acceptNextCardId?: string | null`,
  `rejectNextCardId?: string | null` (`DurationEventCard` inherits them).

  columns into typed fields.

  `hasChoices`, stashes `state.pendingEventChoice` and returns `null`;
  `resolveEventChoice()` implements accept (apply + push `acceptNextCardId`)
  and reject (skip + push `rejectNextCardId`); `pushChainCard()` pushes a
  freshly built instance to the **top** of the incident deck with a
  deterministic serial; `processEndOfTurn()` pauses with

- `MainStreetCommands.ts` — snapshot-based undo/redo of the choice.

### UI

  onAccept, onReject)` (Accept/Reject buttons, no escalation preview, overlay
  depth conventions).
- `scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — shows the dialog when
  `choicePending` is observed; reduced-motion aware.

### AI

  (Easy: always accept; Medium: accept if manageable; Hard: static full-chain
  severity comparison + `AI_EVENT_CHOICE_SIGNIFICANTLY_WORSE_RATIO`).
- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `resolveAiEventChoice()` resolves pending choices

### Tests

- **No static validation tooling** — dangling links only logged at runtime.

2. **Generalise, with a seam**: support an ordered option list while preserving
   legacy accept/reject, behind a documented game-agnostic boundary that can
   later move to `src/core-engine`.
3. **Document** the full lifecycle end to end for content designers and
   developers.
4. **Implement** the tooling (validator, graph/manifest export, authoring

   feedback, continuity indicator).
5. **Test** the hardened model, tooling and player-facing behaviour, and guard

- **Scope risk (epic)** — "implement all improvements now" is broad; the epic

# Intake Brief — Move level label to left (MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327)

## Problem Statement
When a business or community-space card is upgraded it shows a gold level badge
("Lvl 1", "Lvl 2", …) in the **top-right** corner of the card face. This
position competes with the cost circle / right-hand text column and reads as a
secondary stat rather than the card's primary upgrade indicator. The badge
should move to the **top-left** of the card so the upgrade level is immediately
visible in a consistent, expected position.

## Users
- **Main Street player** — wants to identify an upgraded card's level at a
  glance when scanning the street grid and their hand.
- **Future example-game authors / designers** — reuse the shared
  `UpgradeOverlaySpec` contract and expect a single, predictable corner
  convention for the level badge.

### User Stories
- As a player, when I look at an upgraded card on the street or in my hand, I
  see the "Lvl N" badge at the top-left of the card, so the level is obvious at
  a glance.
- As a player, the badge position is identical whether the card is shown on the
  street grid or in the hand, so I never have to re-learn where to look.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For every upgraded card (`level > 0`), the level badge is positioned at
      the card's **top-left**: in container-local coordinates (origin at the
      card centre) `levelBadge.x` is negative (left of centre) and the badge is
      **left-anchored** (`originX === 0`); the badge is no longer placed in the
      top-right (`x` must not be positive in the mirrored position). Verified by
      unit test on `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` for level 1 and level 2 cards.
- [ ] The Phaser renderer (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) renders the badge with a
      left/top origin so the text starts at the top-left inset and remains fully
      inside the card bounds (no clipping past the left or top edge); the same
      overlay path is used by street and hand cards, so both move together.
      Verified by renderer/overlay tests.
- [ ] Badge content and styling are unchanged (`Lvl N`, gold `#ffdd44`, bold,
      10px) and no badge is produced for level 0 (base) cards.
- [ ] The dynamic SVG card-face generator (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits the
      level badge at the top-left (`x` at the card's left inset,
      `text-anchor="start"`) for consistency with the overlay, with its unit
      tests updated accordingly.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
      (notably the module docs in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` /
      `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and the level-badge references in
      `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, with all existing
      top-right level-badge expectations updated to the top-left contract.

## Constraints
- Card geometry is fixed: canonical **140 × 80** card with a **64 × 64 art zone
  at (8, 8)** (top-left) — see `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md`. The
  top-left corner is therefore occupied by the card art; the badge will render
  over the top-left of the art zone (mirroring the current badge overlaying the
  top-right). This is an accepted input to the brief (see Risks & Assumptions).
- Presentation-only change — no change to upgrade rules, card state, or level
  numbers.
- Reuse the existing overlay/badge primitives and gold styling; do not introduce
  new assets or a second badge component.
- Keep the overlay spec a pure data module (no Phaser imports) so it stays
  unit-testable in Node.

## Existing State
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` builds the badge at
  `x = Math.round(width / 2 - 4)`, `y = Math.round(4 - height / 2)` (top-right,
  4 px inset) with `color: '#ffdd44'`, `fontSize: '10px'`, `fontStyle: 'bold'`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) creates the
  Phaser Text and calls `lvlText.setOrigin(1, 0)` — right/top anchored — so the
  badge sits in the top-right.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits
  `<text x="${width - 8}" y="13" … text-anchor="end">Lvl N</text>` (top-right)
  for upgraded cards. (This dynamic SVG path is exercised by unit tests; the
  runtime card face texture comes from the CSV-based template SVGs.)
- Tests asserting/pinning the badge: `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts`
  (positions the badge in the top-right), `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts`
  and `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` (badge presence/text),
  `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` (badge text).

## Desired Change
- Mirror the badge to the top-left: overlay `x = Math.round(-width / 2 + 4)`
  with `originX: 0` (and `setOrigin(0, 0)` in the renderer); `y` stays at the
  existing top inset so the badge remains on the top edge.
- Update the SVG generator badge to `x = 8` (or the chosen left inset) with
  `text-anchor="start"`.
- Update the module/JSDoc comments and the affected tests from "top-right" to
  "top-left". Exact inset values may be tuned during implementation as long as
  the badge is left-anchored in the top-left and stays inside the card bounds.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — level-badge spec `x` / `originX` and the
  "top-right corner" comment; primary change.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays` badge
  `setOrigin(1, 0)` → `(0, 0)`; comment.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — dynamic SVG badge position /
  `text-anchor`; module doc mentions "level badge top-right".
- `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` — update the top-right
  position assertion to top-left and assert left-anchoring.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — badge position/style
  expectations.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — badge presence/absence
  alongside the cash line (position regression surface).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — SVG badge text/position.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — level-badge placement references.

## Related Work
- **Potentially related docs:**
  - `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — canonical 140×80 card and the
    `(8, 8)` 64×64 art zone that occupies the top-left.
  - `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — upgrade level-up burst notes that
    reference the newly-rendered level badge.
  - `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` header — documents the overlay contract
    and the card-local coordinate system.
- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `MS-0MTV69NII000LW8I` — *Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card,
    growing right* (bug, medium) — closest precedent: a card-face overlay
    repositioned from centre/right to left, landed with documented placement
    assumptions.
  - `MS-0MU9JYNZ3008AH5J` — *Update createCoinGrid defaults to left-anchored
    position* (task) — companion implementation task for the sister reposition.
  - `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — *Assign a dedicated 64×64 sprite to every Main
    Street card* (medium) — touches the top-left art zone that the badge will
    now overlay.
  - `MS-0MTRRYOT6001167R` — *Change the name of Physiotherapy business card to
    Physiotherapist* (task, low) — another card-face presentation tweak with
    test/doc churn.
  - Historical (core-repo) references cited in code: `CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN`
    (64×64 left-art layout) and `CG-0MP1VJVEK003I7VE` (display upgrade state on
    street-grid cards) — the layout and overlay these tests assert were
    introduced/refined there.
- **Automated report** (generated by `find-related`) — see the
  "Related work (automated report)" section retained below.

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Assumption:** "top left" means the card's top-left corner, mirroring the
  current right-side inset, with the badge left-aligned. Because the 64×64 art
  zone occupies `(8, 8)`–`(72, 72)`, the badge will overlay the top-left of the
  card art. That is accepted; if the producer finds it illegible over the art, a
  subtle backing chip or a slightly different inset is a small follow-up — it
  must be raised rather than assumed.
- **Visual-regression risk:** the badge colour (`#ffdd44` gold) may have low
  contrast against some card art; mitigate during implementation by checking the
  darkest/lightest card arts and, if needed, a 1 px dark outline (recorded as a
  follow-up if it expands scope).
- **Test churn:** `upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` explicitly asserts a
  top-right position; update the assertions to the top-left contract in the same
  change rather than deleting them.
- **Scope creep:** do not restyle the badge, redesign the 64×64 layout, or
  change the cost circle / title / cash line. Record any broader card-face polish
  as separate work items.

## Open Questions
- None — the seed context (position the upgrade level badge at the top-left
  instead of the top-right) plus repo inspection of the overlay/spec/renderer
  provided sufficient signal for a clear brief. The only judgement call (badge
  overlays the top-left art zone) is recorded above as an assumption to be
  confirmed during review; no clarifying interview was required.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers
- No interview conducted — the work-item description ("When a card is upgraded
  it gets a 'Lvl 1' label. Move this from the current location (top right) to
  the top left.") plus repo inspection of `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`,
  `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, and `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` provided
  sufficient signal to draft a clear brief. No assumptions were left
  unrecorded; see Risks & Assumptions for the documented top-left-art-overlay
  assumption.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** – write storylines (open)
- **MS-0MTIILDBB001F01S** – Competitive Monte Carlo harness: head-to-head simulation (blocked)

# Storyline Coverage Analytics in Monte Carlo Harness

## Problem Statement

The Monte Carlo balance harness (MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts) currently tracks card ownership, market offers, and economy history across simulation runs, but has no visibility into storyline event coverage. Storyline events — which form branching chains with accept/reject choices — are a key game mechanic, yet the harness cannot report how often storylines fire, how deeply their chains progress, whether cycles appear, or what impact storyline choices have on win rates. This leaves the balance team blind to storyline-related balance issues.

## Users

- **Balance team / game designers**: Want to understand whether storylines are contributing positively to the game (e.g., do "Accept" choices correlate with higher win rates? Do certain storylines trigger too or too rarely?).
- **Content designers**: Want to verify that all storylines are being exercised in simulation and that chains progress reasonably (not dead-ending too quickly or cycling excessively).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storyline fire frequency**: The harness reports how many runs and what percentage feature each storyline (`storyline-economy`, `storyline-health`, `storyline-labor`, `storyline-restaurant`, `storyline-tax`), derived from event-choice transcript records captured during simulation runs.

2. **Chain depth tracking**: For each storyline event encountered, the harness tracks how far the chain progresses (number of consecutive chain cards pushed), reported per storyline as a distribution (mean, median, max depth) across runs.

3. **Cycle detection**: The harness detects and counts cycle occurrences (tax → tax-error → tax-inquiry → tax, per `storyline-manifest.json` edges with `cycle: true`), reporting cycle frequency per storyline and per run.

4. **Win-rate impact of choices**: For each storyline with choices (flu-outbreak, popular-menu, recession, strike-service, tax, tax-error, tax-inquiry), the harness computes the win-rate differential between "Accept" and "Reject" choices — similar to existing M2 win-rate delta pattern.

5. **Integration with existing analytics**: Storyline analytics are exposed as new functions in the balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) following the same pattern as existing metrics (G1–G8, M1–M7), with graceful degradation when storyline data is absent.

## Constraints

- **Non-blocking**: This is a deferred enhancement; it must not change existing Monte Carlo harness behaviour (strategies, termination, output format for non-storyline fields).
- **Graceful degradation**: All new storyline metrics return `null` when event-choice data is not available in run summaries (consistent with existing M4/M6/G4/G6/G7 patterns).
- **Builds on existing transcript recording**: The harness already has a lazy `recordMainStreetEvent` call path via `require('./MainStreetTranscript')`; the extension should extend this path to capture event-choice data into a new field on `MonteCarloRunSummary`.
- **No UI changes required**: Output is analytical (JSON/CSV), consistent with existing harness output.

## Existing State

- Monte Carlo harness (`MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`) runs simulations with strategies (market-greedy, demo-greedy, greedy, banking-greedy, random) and records `MonteCarloRunSummary` per seed.
- The harness already records `cardsOwned`, `marketOffers`, and `economyHistory` on run summaries (Phase 1 data).
- Storyline events with choices are resolved in-engine; `recordStorylineResolution` in `MainStreetStoryline.ts` emits `event-choice` transcript events.
- The Monte Carlo harness has a try/catch wrapper for `recordMainStreetEvent` that silently ignores failures when no recorder is wired.
- Storyline manifest (`docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json`) defines 5 storylines, 14 edge transitions, and 1 cycle group.
- Balance engine (`src/scripts/balance/engine/`) has 8 global metrics (G1–G8) and 7 card metrics (M1–M7) with graceful degradation patterns.

## Desired Change

1. **Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary`** with a new field capturing event choices encountered during a run (event ID, choice made, chain depth at that point).
2. **Wire transcript recording** in the Monte Carlo harness so that event-choice events are captured (not just ai-action events).
3. **Add storyline analytics functions** to the balance engine:
   - `computeStorylineFireFrequency(runs)`: percentage of runs per storyline.
   - `computeChainDepthStats(runs)`: depth distribution per storyline.
   - `computeCycleStats(runs)`: cycle frequency per storyline and per run.
   - `computeChoiceWinRateDelta(runs, eventId)`: win-rate difference between Accept vs Reject.
4. **Export storyline metrics** from the balance engine barrel file.
5. **Add tests** covering all new analytics functions.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Extend `MonteCarloRunSummary` interface; wire transcript recording for event-choice events.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/index.ts` — Barrel file for new storyline metrics exports.
- `src/scripts/balance/engine/storyline-metrics.ts` (new) — New analytics module for storyline-specific metrics.
- `tests/main-street/balance/storyline-metrics.test.ts` (new) — Tests for storyline analytics functions.
- `docs/main-street/storyline-manifest.json` — Reference for storyline definitions and cycle edges (read-only).

## Related Work

- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** — write storylines (epic, completed): The parent epic that shipped the storyline system.
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** — Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed): Provides the manifest data model.
- **MS-0MUMP96XH002SJ89** — Named storylines, outcome feedback & continuity indicator (completed): Provides storyline naming and feedback mechanics.
- **MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6** — Static validator & npm gate (completed): Validates storyline integrity.

# Implement free market re-roll mechanic (engine + state + bias draw)

**Summary:** Add the engine logic for the Investor's free market re-roll: per-turn state tracking, the bias-aware draw algorithm, and the integration with the existing market refill path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform one coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it advances the per-turn escalation counter (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a 75% chance to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space synergyTypes; event targetSynergy/effect; staff allowedBusinessTypes overlap with the hosting business's synergy types).
- The biased draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed produces same-game determinism.
- `refillSingleRowMarket` is parameterised to accept the bias/relevance pool; the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- The bias draw preserves the >=1-business row composition invariant.

**Parent Coverage:** Implements parent AC2 (One free re-roll per turn) and parent AC3 (Relevance bias).

**Minimal Implementation:**
- Add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` to state types
- Reset flag at `WeekStart`
- Implement `canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`
- Implement bias-aware draw in `refillSingleRowMarket`
- Wire up the bias detection (hosting business synergy types overlap)

**Dependencies:** Add Investor card to catalog (CSV + types + parsing)

**Deliverables:** Engine functions, state field, bias draw algorithm, WeekStart reset.

**Key Files:**
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` or `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`
